quality.evidence: instruction.md and hireops_rules.md:1-430 support the functional, polish and visual criteria; no verified hidden visual or route constraint found.

functional/judge.toml:105-113 combines arbitrary-ID creation and rescission; :132-141 combines multiple independent validation outcomes; :573-581 combines five anonymous-write protections into binary bars.
quality.counterexample: An app that preserves unusual IDs on creation but fails only their rescission earns zero for hro_offer_identity (functional/judge.toml:105-113). hro_numeric_validation (:132-141) and hro_anon_write (:573-581) also collapse separately useful correct outcomes into one binary score.
quality.suggested_fix: Split independently useful outcomes into separate weighted criteria and reuse shared scenarios as setup.

functional/judge.toml:553-572 grades forged derived claims, while hireops_rules.md:26-34 leaves body field names free; functional/prompt.md:13 limits replay to observed shapes.
quality.counterexample: A vulnerable app trusting an unexposed derived-body alias such as proposedRateCents can pass hro_claim_economics (functional/judge.toml:553-564): no public body field contract exists, and the browser prompt permits only observed request shapes.
quality.suggested_fix: Define public claim keys or narrow the graded bar to observable fields; leave broader arbitrary-body protection as an unscored limitation.
